caveats: ⚑ skill2 trigger unit: kit says "after N normal attack(s)". Drake is SG with hitsPerShot 10, so a hitCount trigger that counts PELLET HITS instead of ROUNDS would fire these riders ~10x too often. Authored as rounds/trigger-pulls (count 10 / count 5); MUST be verified against the engine's hitCount accounting for multi-pellet weapons before trusting any total.

⚑ skill2 first line reads "Affects 3 enemy unit(s) with the lowest remaining HP" — the v1 sim has a single boss, so the 98.55% lands ONCE per activation, not 3x. If the engine ever models multiple enemies this line must fan out to 3 targets.
⚑ Both damage riders default to Full-Burst-by-timing (noFb NOT set) per the standing prior; only the burst nuke is FB-exempt (burst cast resolves before the FB window opens).

⚑ maxAmmoPct stacks on Drake herself during her own Full Burst: skill1's SG-ally +50.14% and burst's self +72.18% co-apply on a 9-round magazine. Whether the engine adds them additively and how it rounds the resulting capacity (9 -> ~20 rounds) is unverified; it directly gates shots fired and therefore damage.

⚑ hitRatePct 20.09 is routed through the engine's Hit-Rate->core lift (hrCoreMult). The kit gives a Hit Rate percentage, NOT a core rate; the conversion magnitude is a measured-only quantity and is the single largest uncertainty in this unit's team contribution.

⚑ crit:true on all three flatDamage riders follows the standing rider-crit prior, not kit text. If the engine's global RIDERCRIT gate already governs rider crit eligibility, these explicit flags are redundant (not additive) — confirm before reading any crit-rate assertion off these hits.
override.note: PARSER BASELINE (HYPOTHESIS — NOT a validated model). Every ⚑ below is an UNMEASURED estimate; hand-tune + record against a real fight before trusting any number. Blind second read of drake (SG/Fire/Attacker/B3) from kit prose only. Structure: skill1 is a pure FB-enter team aura split into a universal leg (Hit Rate + ATK, all allies) and a shotgun-scoped leg (ATK + Max Ammo, alliesOfWeapon SG — Drake is SG so she receives her own second leg). skill2 is two independent normal-attack-count riders (10-attack 98.55% AoE-flavored, 5-attack 201.6% single-target) — both authored as hitCount triggers counting ROUNDS, which is the load-bearing assumption for a 10-pellet shotgun (see caveats). Burst is a single 3009.6% instant nuke on cast (FB-exempt per the burst-cast timing prior) plus a self Max Ammo + Attack Damage window. Weapon-state lines (Max Ammunition Capacity ▲, both legs) are modeled as damage-relevant per the HARD RULES — they gate shots fired on a 9-round magazine with a 111-frame reload, where ammo capacity is unusually leveraged. No kit line is dropped; unmodeled is empty for all three slots. Nothing here has been checked against a board, a probe, or the regression snapshot.

flags.estimate: hitCount 10 and hitCount 5, counting ROUNDS (trigger pulls), not the 10 pellets each SG shot produces
flags.reasoning: Kit says 'normal attack(s)'. In game a shotgun shot is ONE normal attack that sprays 10 pellets. If the engine's hitCount accumulator increments per landed pellet-hit, both riders fire ~10x too often (the 201.6% would proc every half-shot), which would dominate Drake's damage and is globally inconsistent with a 9-round magazine + 111-frame reload — she cannot fire 5 rounds and 10 rounds per magazine cycle often enough for pellet-rate procs to be plausible. This is the single highest-leverage unknown in the file.
flags.recipe: Instrument cfg.onEvent in a scripts/tests/units/drake.test.ts fixture: count damage events with bucket/source attributable to the skill2 riders over a fixed fight, and compare against the count of 'shot' events. Expected ratio if rounds-counted: ~(shots/5 + shots/10). If the observed rider count is ~10x that, the engine is counting pellets and the counts must be scaled (or the engine's SG hit accounting fixed).

flags.estimate: Use the engine's datamined SG cadence unchanged; reload 111 frames = 1.85s at 60fps
flags.reasoning: Cadence tuple is a known-unreliable datamine field (rate_of_fire is nominal, and the game fires on 60fps frame boundaries so effective = 60/ceil(60/nominal)). Drake's whole kit is ammo-economy leveraged (two stacking Max Ammo buffs) and her skill2 riders are shot-count triggered, so BOTH her sustained damage and her rider proc rate are directly proportional to the true effective pulls/sec. A nominal-vs-effective error propagates into every number this override produces.
flags.recipe: Read the effective SG pulls/sec the engine derives and confirm it is 60/ceil(60/nominal), not the raw nominal. Verify against an ammo-counter read on a real Drake recording (the ammo counter measures shots/sec directly; FB-count reads are downstream of gauge and do NOT measure this).

flags.estimate: 20.09 kit percentage passed straight to hrCoreMult; the resulting core-rate lift is UNKNOWN
flags.reasoning: Hit Rate is not a damage stat — its value comes entirely from the accuracy-circle geometry converting hit rate into a higher core-hit fraction. The kit gives the Hit Rate number but nothing about the core lift it produces, and the lift is weapon- and range-band-dependent (an SG team benefits very differently from an AR team). Because this buff hits ALL allies, an error here mis-scales the whole team, not just Drake.
flags.recipe: Toggle HRCORE=0 vs default on a fixed comp containing Drake and diff per-unit core-hit counts and totals; cross-check the implied core-rate delta against the accuracy geometry tables in docs/data/sg-calc/ for the relevant band. Do NOT back-derive the lift from a damage total (that infers the mechanic from its own consequence).

flags.estimate: true (burst nuke excluded from the +50% Full Burst major)
flags.reasoning: Applied from the standing prior that burst-cast instant damage resolves before the Full Burst window opens, so it cannot take the FB major. This is a convention, not a measurement, and it is worth ~50% of a 3009.6% hit — the largest single damage line in the kit. If Drake's burst animation actually lands the AoE after the FB banner, this is a large under-credit.
flags.recipe: Frame-read a Drake burst on real footage anchored to the exact 03:00→02:59 frame: does the big AoE popup appear before or after the Full Burst banner? Alternatively assert in the harness that the nuke's damage event carries inFullBurst=false / fbMajorApplied=false and confirm that matches the footage ordering.

flags.estimate: noFb left OFF (riders take FB by timing); crit:true on all three flatDamage effects
flags.reasoning: Per-kit noFb is measured-only and defaults OFF, so the riders inherit the +50% whenever they happen to land inside a Full Burst window — correct by convention but unverified for Drake specifically. crit:true likewise follows the rider-crit prior rather than kit text; if the engine's global RIDERCRIT gate already makes flat-damage riders crit-eligible, the explicit flag is redundant rather than additive, but if that gate is off these riders would silently never crit.
flags.recipe: Read popup colours for the 98.55%/201.6% procs on real footage (orange + crit icon = critting; white = not) and check whether proc magnitudes step up ~1.5x inside the FB window. In-harness: filter damage events for the rider buckets and assert on their crit/inFullBurst/fbMajorApplied fields.

flags.estimate: Additive during Drake's own Full Burst: 9 × (1 + 0.5014 + 0.7218) ≈ 20 rounds; rounding rule unknown
flags.reasoning: Two co-active Max Ammunition buffs land on Drake simultaneously during a rotation she bursts. Whether the engine sums the percentages or composes them multiplicatively changes the magazine by ~2 rounds, and how it rounds a fractional capacity (floor vs round) changes it by 1 more. On a 9-round base with a 1.85s reload, each extra round is a meaningful fraction of her uptime — this is a shots-fired change, i.e. a damage change.
flags.recipe: Emit reload events for Drake in a harness fixture across a full rotation and read the actual magazine size in and out of her burst window; confirm the composed capacity and the rounding against maxAmmo() in sim.ts.

flags.estimate: One damage instance per activation (single-boss collapse), NOT 3x 98.55%
flags.reasoning: The kit line targets 3 enemies with the lowest remaining HP; the v1 sim models one partless boss, so only one instance can land. Multiplying by 3 to 'represent' the AoE would be fabricating damage that does not exist in the graded single-target scenario. Flagged so the collapse is visible rather than silent — it means this line is worth roughly a third of its nominal kit value relative to a multi-enemy stage.
flags.recipe: No measurement needed for v1 (single boss is a scope-lock fact). Re-open only if the engine ever models multiple enemies, at which point the block needs a real multi-target fan-out.
